title: When the Interior Wakes
premise: Rosalind Marchetti, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost her sense of taste after her father's death, drifts through a life she no longer claims as her own. At his funeral, a stranger named Elias Voss greets the family by the name 'Marchetti'—a name they abandoned decades ago—and leaves behind an old photograph that suggests her father committed a long-buried betrayal. As Rosalind investigates, she uncovers her father's role in destroying a rival family's restaurant and reputation, and finds herself falling for Elias even as he pursues a justice the law can no longer deliver. In the end, Rosalind publicly confesses her father's crime in her final review, forfeits her career, and chooses Elias—not as forgiveness granted but as forgiveness built, reopening a small kitchen where both families' recipes finally share a table.
about_author: Quentin Montrose is the pen name of a former line cook who spent eleven years in professional kitchens before turning to fiction. He writes about appetite, inheritance, and the quiet violence of respectable families from a coastal town he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her writing a glowing review of food she cannot taste, moving through her apartment like a renter. Her father's sudden death summons her home. Emotional beat: numbness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: At the funeral, Elias Voss offers condolences using 'Marchetti,' a surname Rosalind has never heard. Her mother's face goes white. POV: Rosalind. Beat: first crack in the sealed past.

chapters.title: What the Will Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Rosalind sorts her father's study and finds the will oddly specific about a shuttered property on Delancey Street. POV: Rosalind. Beat: curiosity overriding grief for the first time.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Elias appears at the house's gate, leaving an envelope: a 1980s photo of her father with two men outside a restaurant called Voss & Marchetti. POV: alternating Rosalind/Elias. Beat: dread dressed as nostalgia.

chapters.title: Mother's Silence
chapters.summary: Rosalind confronts her mother, who admits only that 'we changed the name for good reasons.' POV: Rosalind. Beat: the family's love revealed as a locked room.

chapters.title: Elias Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV: we learn he has spent years documenting what the Marchettis did to his grandfather's restaurant, but he withholds the worst from Rosalind. Beat: sympathy entangled with calculation.

chapters.title: Delancey Street
chapters.summary: Rosalind visits the boarded property named in the will and finds her father kept it—and paid taxes on it—for forty years. POV: Rosalind. Beat: guilt inherited like furniture.

chapters.title: Taste Returns at the Worst Moment
chapters.summary: Sharing an accidental meal with Elias, Rosalind tastes food for the first time in three years—at his grandmother's recipe. POV: Rosalind. Beat: awakening that feels like betrayal of her grief.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Elias shows Rosalind newspaper clippings: her father's testimony helped revoke the Voss family's licenses and credit, ending them. POV: Elias. Beat: the stranger becomes an accuser.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Drawn together despite everything, Rosalind and Elias nearly cross a line, then retreat—she to loyalty, he to purpose. Dual POV. Beat: desire sharpened by impossibility.

chapters.title: The Mother's Version
chapters.summary: Her mother finally tells her side: the betrayal was survival, not malice—or so she insists. POV: Rosalind. Beat: truth revealed as contested territory.

chapters.title: What Elias Withheld
chapters.summary: Rosalind discovers the document Elias hid: her father didn't just testify—he forged evidence. POV: Rosalind. Beat: the man she mourned dissolves.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Elias proposes restitution: sign Delancey Street over to him and publish nothing, or he goes public and ruins her by association. POV: Elias. Beat: justice curdling into leverage.

chapters.title: Power's Seduction
chapters.summary: Holding the secret, Rosalind feels its corrupting pull—she could bury it, protect her column, her name. POV: Rosalind. Beat: temptation wearing the mask of self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Review She Can't Write
chapters.summary: Her editor demands a career-defining piece; Rosalind sits before a blank page, tasting nothing again. POV: Rosalind. Beat: the old life closing like a door.

chapters.title: Delancey Street, Opened
chapters.summary: Rosalind unlocks the property alone and finds her father's journals inside—confessions he never sent. POV: Rosalind. Beat: the dead finally speak.

chapters.title: Confrontation
chapters.summary: She brings the journals to Elias; he reads his grandfather's ruin in her father's handwriting and breaks down. POV: Elias. Beat: vengeance meeting its own exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Elias must decide whether exposure still means anything now that Rosalind knows everything; Rosalind must decide whether love is possible without absolution. Dual POV. Beat: two people choosing each other over their grievances.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: Rosalind publishes her final review: part confession, part history of Voss & Marchetti, signed with her real name. POV: Rosalind. Beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The fallout: colleagues recoil, her mother stops speaking to her, but strangers write letters about their own buried family debts. POV: Rosalind. Beat: loss and strange lightness coexisting.

chapters.title: The Kitchen on Delancey
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Elias reopen the space as a small restaurant serving both families' recipes, cooking side by side through a hard first service. POV: alternating. Beat: labor as reconciliation.

chapters.title: When the Interior Wakes
chapters.summary: Months later, Rosalind tastes her father's last recorded dish, cooked from his journal, and forgives him aloud to an empty dining room. Elias takes her hand. POV: Rosalind. Beat: grace arriving without permission, on time after all.
